papers.title: Lamina Cribrosa Strain as a Glaucoma Prognostic Factor: The STRAIN Study Methodology and Initial Outcomes
papers.abstract: Objective: To estimate the lamina cribrosa (LC) strain response to intraocular pressure (IOP) change in open angle glaucoma (OAG) patients and examine associations between LC strain and demographic and clinical characteristics relevant to OAG in an ongoing longitudinal study. Design: Cohort study Participants: Adult patients with OAG (205 eyes of 119 patients) Methods: The STRAIN study is an ongoing longitudinal study designed to determine whether LC biomechanical strain is associated with present, prior, and future OAG damage. In this initial analysis, patients either temporarily stopped [≥] 1 eye drop, initiated an eye drop, or underwent selective laser trabeculoplasty to produce IOP change. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans of the optic nerve head (ONH) acquired before and up to several weeks after IOP change were analyzed using digital volume correlation (DVC) to estimate LC strain. Strain measurements were compared with age, race, sex, axial length, central corneal thickness (CCT), corneal hysteresis, optic disc area, years of known OAG, retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness, and visual field mean deviation (MD). Main Outcome Measures: LC strain estimated by DVC from OCT scans acquired before and after IOP alteration. Results: Axial LC strain (Ezz) was tensile with IOP decrease and compressive with IOP increase. Maximum principal strain was tensile (mean Emax = 1.09%), and maximum shear strain was positive (mean{Gamma} max = 1.16%) in the radial-axial plane. Both increased quadratically with the IOP change. Older age was significantly related to greater tensile circumferential strain (p = 0.02) and lower{Gamma} max (p = 0.01). Sex, CCT, corneal hysteresis, and optic disc area were not significantly associated with LC strain. In combined multivariable models adjusting for IOP change, demographics, and accounting for correlations between eyes from the same patient, eyes with thinner inferior-quadrant RNFL had smaller{Gamma} max for a given IOP change (p = 0.02). Conclusions: LC strain in patients with OAG is associated with the degree of neuronal loss, age, and axial length, supporting a relationship between the LC biomechanical response and factors relevant to glaucomatous damage.

papers.title: Applications of Fairness Training in Artificial Intelligence to Ophthalmic Disease Diagnosis using External Eye Photographs
papers.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR), age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and glaucoma are leading causes of preventable blindness, yet whether external eye photographs carry phenotypic information about posterior segment disease remains unclear, and methods to mitigate demographic disparities in such models are largely unexplored. We developed and evaluated deep learning and vision-language models for binary classification of vision-threatening DR (VTDR), advanced AMD, and glaucoma using 40,687 external eye photographs from 9,878 patients at Massachusetts Eye and Ear. Convolutional networks (WResNet, EfficientNet), a vision transformer (ViT), and a fine-tuned vision-language model (LLaVA) were assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with fairness across sex, race, and ethnicity quantified by the equity-scaled AUC (ES-AUC). Five fairness-training strategies were applied to the best models. LLaVA achieved the highest baseline AUC for VTDR (85.4%, comparable to ViT 82.6%); advanced AMD was similar across architectures (EfficientNet 86.3%; LLaVA 84.8%; ViT 84.7%), whereas glaucoma was substantially worse (67-74%). Fairness training improved VTDR and AMD AUCs to 86.3% and 85.9% while partially mitigating demographic disparities. In summary, although AI models that rely on external eye photography to detect posterior segment disease may not yet be suitable for clinical deployment, the fairness methods demonstrated in this proof-of-concept study could be applied to other AI systems to decrease performance disparities and potentially improve model performance.

papers.title: Retinopathy is more common, but age-related macular degeneration carries more visual impairment: a cross-sectional study of US adults graded from the same fundus photographs
papers.abstract: Background Retinopathy and age-related macular degeneration (AMD) are the most common findings on fundus photographs of older adults, yet their frequency, correlates and visual consequences have been estimated in separate samples. We compared them in a national survey that graded both from the same images. Methods We analyzed 5593 adults aged >=40 years in the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2005-2008 with photographs gradable for both conditions. We estimated survey-weighted prevalence, fitted identically specified logistic models for retinopathy (participants with diabetes) and AMD (full sample), and compared presenting visual impairment (better-eye acuity worse than 20/40) and self-rated vision across four groups: neither condition, retinopathy only, AMD only, and both. Results Retinopathy was more prevalent than AMD (9.54% [95% confidence interval (CI) 8.52-10.56] vs 6.52% [5.54-7.50]); AMD overtook it only from age 70 years. In participants with diabetes, retinopathy was associated with HbA1c (odds ratio [OR] 1.54 per percentage point; 1.33-1.78) and male sex (1.54; 1.10-2.17). AMD was associated with age (OR 1.09 per year; 1.07-1.11) and was less common in non-Hispanic Black adults (0.48; 0.33-0.71). Presenting impairment affected 4.91% of participants with neither condition, 7.09% with retinopathy only, 14.57% with AMD only and 26.15% with both. After age adjustment, impairment remained associated with AMD only (OR 2.23; 1.54-3.23) and both conditions (4.09; 2.28-7.37) but not retinopathy only (1.32; 0.91-1.90). Neither retinopathy nor diabetes was associated with AMD. Self-rated vision agreed poorly with measured impairment (kappa = 0.15): only 12% of impaired participants rated their vision poor or very poor. Conclusions Retinopathy is the more frequent retinal finding in US adults aged >=40 years, but AMD carries more of the measured visual impairment, independently of age. Grading diabetic screening photographs for AMD, and measuring acuity rather than asking about vision, would reach more people who see poorly. Keywords Retinopathy; Diabetic retinopathy; Age-related macular degeneration; Visual impairment; Self-reported vision; Prevalence; NHANES; Cross-sectional studies

papers.title: Time at the curb, not the rate of head scanning, distinguishes street crossing in virtual reality with severe-to-profound visual impairment
papers.abstract: Purpose: We tested whether people with severe-to-profound visual impairment compensate at street crossings with more head scanning and/or more time at the curb. Methods: Ten normally sighted controls, tested with normal vision and with Bangerter filters simulating severe-to-profound visual impairment (approximately 20/2000), and 17 adults with severe-to-profound visual impairment crossed a virtual street in a head-mounted display. Four complexity levels ranged from an empty street to yielding vehicles with pedestrian avatars; only the two most complex levels contained moving vehicles. Cumulative absolute head yaw and latency to step-off were analyzed with mixed-effects models, and latencies were fitted with an ex-Gaussian distribution. Results: Compared with normal vision, latency to step-off was 1.57 times longer with simulated and 1.82 times longer with clinical severe-to-profound visual impairment (Bonferroni p < 0.001 and p = 0.008, respectively). In severe-to-profound visual impairment, the additional latency was attributable to the slow tail of the latency distribution (exponential component {tau} longer by 3.40 s without and 6.20 s with moving vehicles; Bonferroni p = 0.037 and 0.022, respectively); peak position did not differ significantly. Before step-off, cumulative absolute head yaw increased with complexity, F(3, 115.8) = 37.16, p < 0.001, and was 1.88 times higher with simulated impairment than with normal vision (Bonferroni p = 0.024); it did not differ significantly between clinical impairment and normal vision, either before step-off or during walking (both Bonferroni p [≥] 0.479). During walking, its increase with complexity depended on viewing condition, F(6, 109.3) = 5.23, p < 0.001. Conclusions: Severe-to-profound visual impairment was associated with longer and more variable time at the curb, without a significant increase in cumulative head scanning, although the increase in head scanning with complexity during walking was attenuated. Time at the curb is relevant to orientation and mobility practice and accessible crossing design.

papers.title: Efficacy and Clinical Predictors of Topical NSAIDs as Bridging Therapy for Diabetic Macular Edema: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
papers.abstract: Introduction & ObjectivesDiabetic Macular Edema (DME) is a primary cause of vision loss. While anti-VEGF injections are the gold standard, prolonged referral delays in primary care settings often lead to irreversible photoreceptor damage. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of topical Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs (NSAIDs) as a temporary bridging therapy and to develop a new clinical scoring system to guide primary care physicians in early intervention. MethodsA systematic review was conducted to identify clinical predictors of responses to topical NSAIDs in DME patients, followed by a meta-analysis to calculate pooled Odds Ratios (OR) for each predictor. These values underwent natural log transformation ({beta} = ln(OR)) to derive a point-based clinical scoring system. ResultTwelve studies were analyzed. Predictor variables and assigned points derived from pooled ORs included: glycemic control (HbA1c 6/12; OR 1.96, 7 points), and retinopathy stage (mild-to-moderate NPDR; OR 1.77, 5 points). The proposed 28-point scoring system categorizes patients into three tiers: High Probability (21-28 points) for immediate NSAID initiation; Moderate Probability (12-20 points) for combined systemic optimization; and Low Probability (0-11 points) for prioritized emergency referral. Evidence confirms that potent topical NSAIDs effectively stabilize macular thickness and prevent exudative progression during the referral window. ConclusionThis study concludes that the OR-derived scoring system effectively empowers primary care physicians to manage DME during referral windows. Topical NSAIDs serve as a safe, low-risk bridging strategy to mitigate permanent vision loss and reduce the burden of blindness in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Scleral Allograft-Reinforced Cyclodialysis Combined with Phacoemulsification or Performed as a Standalone Procedure: 24-Month Outcomes from the Multicenter CREST Study
papers.abstract: IntroductionAcellular scleral allograft-reinforced cyclodialysis is a bio-interventional surgery (BIOS) to lower intraocular pressure (IOP). We report 2-year efficacy and safety outcomes when the procedure is performed in combination with phacoemulsification and as a standalone procedure in eyes with open-angle glaucoma. MethodsAnalysis of the multicenter CREST real-world evidence study of eyes undergoing allograft-reinforced cyclodialysis with AlloFlo Uveo (Iantrek, Inc., White Plains, NY; NCT05506423). Eyes attending the Month-24 visit were analyzed: 176 eyes undergoing phaco-combined surgery (Cohort 1) and 32 standalone eyes (Cohort 2). Values recorded after secondary procedures censored. Cohort 1 only was stratified by low, moderate, or high baseline IOP ([≤] 15, 16-20, [≥] 21 mmHg). ResultsA total of 176 eyes in Cohort 1 and 32 in Cohort 2 were analyzed. In Cohort 1, IOP decreased 3.1 mmHg at Month 24 from a baseline of 18.0 (-12.5%; p < 0.001), and medications decreased 0.5 from 1.5 (p < 0.001); medication-free eyes rose from 22.9% to 46.4% (p < 0.001). IOP changes in the low, moderate, and high baseline tiers were +0.9 (+7.8%), -3.0 (-16.3%), and -9.2 (-36.1%) mmHg; medication changes were -0.8, -0.6, and +0.1. In Cohort 2, IOP decreased 6.4 mmHg from 20.0 (-27.1%; p < 0.001), and medications decreased 1.2 from 2.8 (p = 0.004); medication-free eyes rose from 4.3% to 30.4% (p = 0.031). Secondary IOP-lowering procedures were performed in 5.1% of Cohort 1 eyes and 28.1% of Cohort 2. Kaplan-Meier freedom from reoperation was 98.9% and 84.4%. No eye developed clinically significant hypotony or choroidal effusion, and there were no allograft-related vision-threatening adverse events. ConclusionAllograft-reinforced cyclodialysis effectively lowered IOP and medication use through 24 months. Trial RegistrationClinicalTrials.gov NCT05506423. Plain Language SummaryGlaucoma damages the optic nerve, usually because pressure inside the eye is too high. A newer operation opens a small channel to a natural drainage route inside the eye and holds it open with thin pieces of biocompatible donor tissue. It spares the surface of the eye, so other operations remain possible later. We asked how well the procedure works after two years. We studied 208 eyes at 17 centers that returned for their two-year visit: 176 done with cataract surgery and 32 done as a standalone procedure. We measured eye pressure and drop use and checked for long-term safety. With cataract surgery, pressure decreased from about 18 to 15 mmHg (millimeters of mercury, the standard measurement for eye pressure) and drop use by about half a drop; eyes starting at the highest pressures improved most, falling about 9 mmHg. Done alone, pressure decreased from about 20 to 14 mmHg and drop use by about one drop. The share of eyes needing no drops at all roughly doubled with cataract surgery, from about a quarter to about a half, and rose from almost none to about a third when done alone. No eye developed dangerously low pressure or fluid behind the retina. About one-in-four eyes treated alone needed a further pressure-lowering procedure within two years, against about one-in-twenty treated with cataract surgery. The procedure meaningfully lowered pressure and drop use over two years without the complications that ended earlier versions of this promising surgery. Key Summary PointsO_ST_ABSWhy carry out this study?C_ST_ABSO_LIEyes needing cataract surgery with better pressure control, and eyes needing pressure control alone, are managed very differently, yet 2-year data on allograft-reinforced cyclodialysis in both settings have not been reported together. C_LIO_LIWe asked: how much do pressure and medication burden fall by 24 months in each setting, how often further surgery is needed, and how safe is it? C_LI What was learned from the study?O_LIWhen performed at the same time as cataract surgery, pressure decreased 3.1 mmHg and medications by 0.5, and the reductions rose steeply with baseline pressure. The proportion of eyes on no glaucoma medication doubled, from 22.9% to 46.4%. C_LIO_LIWhen performed as a standalone procedure, pressure decreased 6.4 mmHg and medications by 1.2, and medication-free eyes rose from 4.3% to 30.4%, reflecting promising outcomes in refractory eyes. C_LIO_LINo eye developed clinical hypotony, choroidal effusion, or corneal decompensation, and endothelial cell loss was confined to the phacoemulsification-combined cohort. Freedom from reoperation at 24 months was 98.9% with cataract surgery and 84.4% standalone. C_LI

papers.title: Accuracy and precision of visual acuity tests: A systematic review and meta-analysis across testing strategies
papers.abstract: PurposeVisual acuity (VA) testing has expanded from examiner-guided to examinee self-guided assessments, yet measurement variability may limit clinical utility. This meta-analysis investigated VA-tests intertest and test-retest accuracy and precision across different testing strategies. MethodsFollowing PRISMA guidelines, we searched PubMed, Google Scholar, and Scopus for VA validation studies published between 1 January 1983 to 02 December 2024. Eligible studies reported intertest or test-retest Bland-Altman mean bias and limits of agreement (LoA); objective VA assessments and correlation coefficient only studies were excluded. Testing strategies were classified by test site, optotype sampling methods, response input methods, and level of supervision. Accuracy outcomes were reported as mean biases. Precision outcomes were reported as intertest LoA half-width and test-retest coefficient of repeatability (CoR) for test-retest. Multilevel random-effects models accounted for multiple estimates per study. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. ResultsAcross 82 included studies (10,873 participants), pooled intertest and test-retest mean biases were both 0.01 logMAR. Intertest LoA half-width was 0.19 logMAR and test-retest CoR was 0.14 logMAR. Variability showed marginal difference by optotype sampling (adaptive: LoA half-width 0.20 logMAR, CoR 0.15 logMAR; fixed: 0.18, 0.13) or response input method (examiner: 0.19, 0.13; self-run: 0.19, 0.18). Only few studies reported results for test site and level of supervision, hence only intertest was compared (test site, clinic: LoA half-width 0.19 logMAR vs remote 0.27 logMAR and level of supervision, supervised: 0.19 logMAR vs unsupervised 0.26 logMAR). QUADAS-2 identified patient selection as the domain of greatest bias concern. ConclusionAcross testing strategies, VA assessments showed minimal systematic bias but substantial variability. Lack of precision is more notable in remote and unsupervised testing while no difference within optotype sampling and response-input methods. Future development should prioritize on improving precision of visual acuity tests with finer adaptive optotype resolution and remote/unsupervised testings through repeatability studies.

papers.title: Effect of Intensity Discretization on Radiomic Features in En Face EDI-OCT of Choroidal Nevi
papers.abstract: Background/ObjectivesIntensity discretization influences radiomic measurements, but its effects in optical coherence tomography (OCT) of choroidal lesions remain insufficiently characterized. We evaluated fixed bin width (FBW) and fixed bin number (FBN) strategies with different parameters to inform discretization choices for en face enhanced-depth imaging OCT (EDI-OCT) of stable choroidal nevi. MethodsNinety-three original-domain radiomic features were extracted from 64 eyes across 11 discretization settings (FBW 2-64; FBN 8-64). We assessed feature values, eye rankings, observer reproducibility, slab-depth dependence, redundancy, and feature-set overlap. Primary absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) used per-eye feature values averaged across six numeric slabs. Histogram entropy and an approximate co-occurrence sampling-density proxy characterized the discretized intensity representation. ResultsSeventy-seven features depended on discretization. Median occupied gray levels decreased with increasing bin width from 54 at FBW 2 to five at FBW 25. Eye rankings were similar between neighboring settings (median Spearman{rho} , 0.97-0.99), but less concordant in selected FBW-FBN comparisons. Median observer ICCs ranged from 0.84 to 0.91, without clear evidence of differences between settings. Feature sets overlapped less after redundancy reduction. FBW 4 and FBN 32 provided intermediate gray-level resolution and sampling-density proxies, retaining at least 16 occupied gray levels in approximately 99% and 100% of observations, respectively. ConclusionsIntensity discretization substantially alters radiomic texture values, eye rankings, and feature selection. Observer reproducibility alone is insufficient to guide discretization choice. Intensity representation, gray-level compression, and slab depth should also be considered. FBW 4 and FBN 32 emerged as exploratory candidate settings within the evaluated pipeline. External validation and assessment of clinical utility remain necessary.

papers.title: Ophthalmic AI With Just Ten Examples: Comparing Multimodal Large Language Models, Vision Foundation Models, and Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: PurposeTo compare multimodal large language models (MLLMs), vision foundation models (VFMs), and contrastive vision-language models (VLMs) for ophthalmic image interpretation with no labeled examples (zero-shot) or as few as 10 labeled examples per class (10-shot). DesignRetrospective benchmarking study. Subjects4 public datasets (UCSD, IDRiD, REFUGE, ASOCT-MSDC) and 3 private datasets (OHTS, BPEI-DLS, WashU-OCT) of anterior-and posterior-segment ophthalmic imaging. MethodsNine AI models were evaluated across 3 architectural families: MLLMs (Qwen3.8-27B, GLM-5.3-Flash, Gemma-4-31B-it), VFMs (DINOv3, RETFound, VisionFM), and VLMs (CLIP, EyeCLIP, SigLIP2). Models were assessed on disease classification, disease risk and severity grading, anatomical assessment, and lesion localization in fundus and OCT imaging. MLLMs were also compared with a 3D VFM (OCTCube-M) for whole-volume OCT classification. MLLMs were evaluated zero-shot and 10-shot, without additional training. Vision models (VFMs and VLMs) were adapted by linear probing and fine-tuning on the same 10-shot set and on the full training dataset (FD). Main Outcome MeasuresDisease classification performance (macro-averaged F1, AUROC, quadratic weighted kappa [QWK]), anatomical localization accuracy, and cross-dataset generalization. ResultsFor retinal OCT disease classification, 10-shot MLLMs achieved a macro-F1 of 0.94, versus 0.59 (10-shot) and 0.96 (FD) for vision models. For diabetic retinopathy and macular edema grading, 10-shot MLLMs achieved QWKs of 0.69 and 0.73, versus 0.48 and 0.57 (10-shot) and 0.72 and 0.79 (FD) for vision models. For lesion localization, 10-shot MLLMs achieved an F1 of 0.75, versus 0.70 (10-shot) and 0.86 (FD) for vision models. For vertical cup-to-disc ratio estimation (OHTS), zero-shot MLLMs achieved a mean absolute error of 0.14, versus 0.21 (10-shot) for vision models. For whole-volume OCT classification (WashU-OCT), zero-shot MLLMs achieved a macro-F1 of 0.71, versus 0.50 (10-shot) and 0.82 (FD) for vision models. ConclusionsOpen-weight MLLMs given 10 labeled examples per class outperformed VFMs and VLMs trained on the same examples in most tasks and approached the performance of fully trained VFMs and VLMs in selected disease classification and grading tasks. MLLMs also demonstrated promising zero-shot performance on non-public clinical datasets without task-specific training. By reducing the need for large labeled datasets and task-specific model adaptation, MLLMs could broaden who can develop and validate ophthalmic AI.

papers.title: Evaluation of a Novel Intervention for Individuals at High Risk for Blindness from Diabetic Retinopathy: the SEEN Program Pilot
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of the Sight-Saving Engagement and Evaluation in New Haven (SEEN) Program, designed to engage individuals at high risk for diabetic retinopathy (DR) in eye care. Study Setting and DesignIn this single-arm, nonrandomized, prospective intervention at a tertiary-care-affiliated institution in the Northeastern US, we enrolled 35 adults with diabetes at highest-quartile risk for DR, with no eye exam in the preceding year. Participants underwent comprehensive eye examination, DR education, and one year of social needs navigation by a community partner. We conducted a multi-method evaluation assessing program feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary clinical outcomes over 12 months. We thematically analyzed semi-structured interviews with participants, research team, and key partners. We organized themes using the RE-AIM, SEEN screening determinants, and Tailored Implementation in Chronic Diseases frameworks. Data Sources and Analytic SampleWe collected surveys and electronic health record data from participants between July 2022 and September 2024. We conducted one-on-one interviews to understand the experience of the program between July 2024 and October 2024. Principal FindingsWe enrolled 26.5% of eligible individuals. Of 35 participants, 30 (85.7%) completed baseline social needs assessment, 25 (71.4%) completed the program, and 15 (42.9%) had underwent a follow-up eye exam. Patient navigators identified 31 social needs among 22 participants (62.9%). They spent a mean 96.8 (SD 43.8) minutes navigating participants over 12 months. Only two needs (6.5%) remained unresolved or unmet. HbA1c decreased among study completers (9.8 to 8.5; p=0.03). From 20 interviews, we identified 10 themes in 4 categories: feasibility (implementation, adaptive strategies, opportunities), acceptability (team dynamics, interpersonal interaction, procedural interface), appropriateness (external context, emotional context), and effectiveness (resources provided, lifestyle impact). ConclusionsPilot results support the feasibility and acceptability of the SEEN model to engage individuals at high risk for DR in eye care. Callout BoxWhat is known on this topic O_LIDiabetic retinopathy is a leading cause of preventable blindness in the US, but screening adherence is suboptimal, particularly among marginalized populations. C_LIO_LIPatient navigation programs for other chronic diseases can facilitate engagement in care, and may be a component of successful programs to improve adherence to care for patients with increased support needs. C_LI What this study found O_LIA program that risk-stratifies patients to provide high-touch education and social needs navigation shows promise for reducing barriers to diabetic retinopathy care and increasing eye exam utilization. C_LIO_LIFeedback from participants, key partners, and research team found the program feasible and acceptable C_LI

papers.title: Beyond Billing Codes: An Agentic Large Language Model Pipeline for Extracting Glaucoma Procedural Data from Free-Text Clinical Notes
papers.abstract: PurposeTo evaluate the accuracy of a large language model (LLM)-based agentic workflow to extract procedural data from free-text glaucoma clinical notes in the electronic health record (EHR). DesignCross-sectional. Subjects1,250 subjects in the Bascom Palmer Ophthalmic Repository. MethodsRandomly sampled clinical notes from glaucoma encounters dated 2014 to 2024 were labeled by two glaucoma specialists (with an adjudicator as needed) for prior glaucoma-related procedures (name, date, details) and recommended future procedures (name, details). Notes were split into development (10%), validation (10%), and test (80%) sets. Five LLMs (Claude Opus 4.6, DeepSeek-V4 Pro, GPT-5.5, Grok 4.1, and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) were accessed in Microsoft Foundry through HIPAA-compliant containers. The extraction pipeline comprised a three-step agentic workflow (extraction, validation, and conditional revision) followed by text standardization. Detection of procedure data was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score. Among positive cases, performance was evaluated using exact-match accuracy and Jaccard Index (JI). Prior procedure labels were also compared with EHR glaucoma-related Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes. Main Outcome MeasuresAccuracy, exact-match accuracy, JI. ResultsA total of 1,984 (992 notes x 2 eyes) labels were evaluated for each task in the test set. Prior and future procedures were identified in 1,057 (53.3%) and 152 (7.7%) eyes, respectively. Accuracy ranged from 0.965 (Grok) to 0.996 (Claude) for prior procedures and 0.969 (DeepSeek, Qwen)-0.978 (Claude) for future procedures. Among positive cases, exact-match accuracy ranged from 0.681 (Grok) to 0.890 (Claude) for prior procedures and 0.704 (Grok)-0.849 (Claude) for future procedures; JI ranged from 0.827 (Grok) to 0.956 (Claude) and 0.734 (Grok) to 0.883 (Claude), respectively. Among all 1,760 prior procedures present in adjudicated labels, only 441 (25.1%) were captured by CPT-coded EHR data. ConclusionsA secure agentic LLM pipeline accurately extracted glaucoma procedural data from clinical notes, recovering data largely absent from structured EHR fields. Claude performed best across both tasks. Limited agreement between labels and CPT codes likely reflects procedures performed at outside institutions and the limited granularity of CPT coding. This approach may support a scalable, comprehensive characterization of procedure burden among glaucoma patients for research and clinical applications.

papers.title: Visual acuity after proton beam therapy for uveal melanoma: development and validation of a prediction model
papers.abstract: AimTo develop proton beam therapy treatment planning dose constraints for uveal melanoma (UM), more knowledge is needed on the impact of dose on toxicity. Here, we identify risk factors and develop prediction models for lower post-therapeutic visual acuity. MethodsLUMC patients treated at Holland PTC between 2020-2023 (n=135) and at PSI between 1987-2019 (n=100) for UM were included. Candidate predictors for severe and moderate to severe vision impairment (Snellen <0.1 and <0.3) were established through literature review and expert interviews and selected through univariable analysis. Multivariable Cox models were fitted on a randomly selected 2/3rd of the combined dataset (n=156). Performance of both models was calculated on the training set and on the held-out validation set (n=79). ResultsThe final models included baseline visual acuity, ciliary body dose and tumour location for both visual acuity cut-offs, supplemented by the optic disk dose and T-stage for visual acuity <0.1 and macula dose for visual acuity <0.3. Internal performance was good (c-indices 0.760 and 0.761 for visual acuity <0.1 and <0.3, respectively). In the held-out validation set, performance was acceptable (c-indices 0.657 and 0.689) and calibration was insufficient for the model predicting visual acuity <0.1, but acceptable for the model predicting visual acuity <0.3. ConclusionWe developed a model predicting moderate to severe visual impairment with good internal performance and acceptable discrimination and calibration on a held-out test set. This is an important step towards NTCP modelling and the development of dose constraints for ocular proton therapy.

papers.title: Natural interaction based visual field prediction in virtual reality - a pilot study
papers.abstract: ObjectiveThe aim was to develop and evaluate the Passive Visual Field Measurement (PVFM), a novel visual field (VF) measurement tool that predicts the VF from a users natural, intuitive interactions in a virtual reality (VR) environment. Due to the flexible nature of its input, the tool could be integrated with various interactive VR tasks and even run passively in the background of tasks users are already motivated to carry out, such as preventive exercises or rehabilitation training. MethodsThe PVFM was developed and compared to a conventional VF measurement method, kinetic perimetry using the Octopus 900 perimeter, in a pilot study with n=4 retinitis pigmentosa patients. Both measurements were carried out for each eye, for a total of eight sets. The measured VFs were compared using radial-weighted Intersection over Union (IoU), showing the degree to which PVFM results align with conventional VF testing. ResultsFor patients with largely concentric visual fields (n=6 eyes), agreement between PVFM and kinetic perimetry was high, with radial-weighted IoU of 75.4% to 91.0% and mean absolute angular distances between VF boundaries of 0.31{degrees} to 2.68{degrees}. In contrast, one patient with pronounced peripheral visual field areas (n=2 eyes) showed substantially lower agreement, with IoU of 29.6% to 35.7% and distances of 17.5{degrees} to 22.3{degrees}, as kinetic perimetry detected a larger peripheral visual area than PVFM. PVFM takes significantly longer than kinetic perimetry, however patient feedback indicates that PVFM is more enjoyable and engaging. ConclusionThe preliminary evidence of this pilot study suggests the feasibility of PVFM as an intuitive and engaging method for detecting VF boundaries in patients with concentric peripheral visual field loss, with agreement with kinetic perimetry within the range of test-retest variability reported for conventional kinetic perimetry. However, PVFM showed drastically lower agreement in peripheral, non-concentric visual field areas, a current limitation requiring further investigation and refinement.

papers.title: Patient-level consequences of local updates to retinal AI for diabetic retinopathy screening: a retrospective two-cohort evaluation
papers.abstract: ObjectivesTo assess whether local artificial intelligence updates for diabetic retinopathy screening that improve image-level probabilities also improve patient-level detection, flagging and net benefit. MethodsThis retrospective evaluation used four systems, BRSET source data and two external cohorts, mBRSET and DeepDRiD, with separate audit and evaluation patients. Updates were fitted and selected on audits of 25-200 patients; probability recalibration and operating policies were selected separately. Outcomes included Brier loss, patient detection, flags and net benefit at four threshold probabilities (p=0.05-0.30). Comparators were no update, flag all and flag none. Conditional patient-cluster intervals compared updates with no update; simple-policy comparisons were descriptive. ResultsAt audit budget 200, mean Brier loss improved in all eight cohort-system comparisons. In mBRSET, flags rose from 154-442 to 809-951 per 1,000 patients and missed positives fell from 51-133 to 2-14 (5.69-9.48 additional flags per additional detection). In mBRSET at p=0.05, three of four updates had lower mean net benefit than flag all; at p=0.20, all four exceeded flag all but remained below no update. In DeepDRiD at p=0.20, the APTOS update increased mean net benefit by 0.0510 over no update and exceeded both simple policies. DiscussionImage-level improvement did not ensure patient-level benefit. Flag increases were consistent with image-level targets applied to patients with about four images. ConclusionLocal updates should be judged on patient-level detection, flags and net benefit against unchanged, flag-all and flag-none policies, not on image-level metrics alone. KEY MESSAGESO_ST_ABSWhat is already known on this topicC_ST_ABSO_LIRetinal AI performance can change between settings, and local recalibration or threshold adjustment can improve conventional evaluation metrics. C_LI What this study addsO_LILocal updates improved image-level Brier loss in all eight cohort-system comparisons, but in mBRSET at p=0.20 all four lowered mean patient-level net benefit, adding 5.7-9.5 positive flags per additional detection. Whether an update outperformed the unchanged, flag-all and flag-none policies depended on the cohort and threshold probability. C_LI How this study might affect research, practice or policyO_LIBefore adopting a local update, services can compare patient detection, positive flags and net benefit with the unchanged, flag-all and flag-none policies on held-out patients. C_LI

papers.title: Longitudinal Modeling of Intraocular Pressure and Its Associated Factors Among Glaucoma Patients: Evidence from Jimma University Medical Center
papers.abstract: BackgroundGlaucoma remains one of the leading causes of irreversible blindness worldwide, and elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) is an important modifiable risk factor for disease progression. Monitoring changes in IOP over time is therefore essential for glaucoma management. However, evidence on the longitudinal trajectory of IOP and its associated factors remains limited in resource-limited settings. This study investigated the longitudinal trajectory of IOP and its associated demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical determinants among glaucoma patients at Jimma University Medical Center. ObjectiveTo assess the longitudinal trajectory of IOP and identify demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical factors associated with changes in IOP among glaucoma patients at Jimma University Medical Center. MethodA retrospective longitudinal study was conducted among glaucoma patients who had at least three follow-up visits at Jimma University Medical Center. Repeated IOP measurements were obtained over six follow-up waves from January 2022 to January 2024. Profile plots were used to describe the longitudinal pattern of IOP, and linear mixed-effects models were fitted to assess factors associated with baseline IOP and changes in IOP over time. Separate models were fitted for the left and right eyes, in addition to a bivariate model that jointly accounted for both eyes. ResultsIOP generally declined over follow-up period, although the magnitude and rate of decline varied across patient characteristics and treatment groups. In the right Eye, rural residence was associated with lower baseline IOP, while occupation and treatment regimen were also significantly associated with baseline IOP. Significant time-by-occupation and time-by-treatment interactions were observed. In particular, right-eye IOP declined more rapidly among patients receiving Timolol with Diamox and Timolol with Xolamol. In the left eye, sex, occupation, treatment regimen, and treatment duration were associated with baseline IOP, while significant interactions between time and Timolol with Latanoprost and short treatment duration were observed. A bivariate model similarly showed significant effects of residence, occupation, and treatment regimen, as well as significant time-by-treatment interactions, indicating different longitudinal IOP trajectories across treatment groups. ConclusionIOP trajectories differed between the two eyes, with a significant decline in left-eye IOP but no significant overall temporal change in right-eye IOP. Treatment regimen was the most consistent factor associated with differences in the longitudinal trajectory of IOP, while occupation, residence, and treatment duration also showed significant associations in selected analyses. These findings highlight the importance of longitudinal monitoring and consideration of patient and treatment characteristics when assessing IOP among glaucoma patients. Further longitudinal studies with larger and more diverse populations are warranted to investigate additional behavioral, environmental, and clinical factors influencing IOP trajectories.

papers.title: Beyond the Index: Association of AI-CO Central Image Area with Central Visual Field Damage in Glaucoma
papers.abstract: PurposeTo evaluate the associations of the numerical AI-CO center index and visually classified central dark-area extent with Humphrey 10-2 mean deviation (MD). MethodsThis single-center retrospective study included 320 eyes of 169 patients with AI-CO imaging, broad-field 24-2F or 30-2 testing, and 10-2 testing. Both visual field examinations were performed within 365 days before or after AI-CO imaging. Two ophthalmologists independently classified central dark-area extent into five Levels (0-4). Analyses assessed Spearman correlations, areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs), distributions across final central dark-area Levels, and interrater reliability. Patient-cluster bootstrap confidence intervals and a one-eye-per-patient sensitivity analysis addressed inclusion of both eyes. ResultsAI-CO center correlated with 10-2 MD ({rho}=0.829; 95% CI, 0.773-0.873). AUCs for 10-2 MD below -2, -6, and -12 dB were 0.902, 0.939, and 0.961, respectively. The numbers of eyes in Levels 0-4 were 66, 57, 94, 53, and 50; median 10-2 MD values were -0.59, -1.48, -3.54, -6.24, and -18.15 dB, respectively. Quadratic-weighted kappa was 0.970 (95% CI, 0.958-0.981). Sensitivity analyses yielded broadly similar findings. ConclusionsThe numerical AI-CO center index and visually classified central dark-area extent were associated with central visual field damage. Assessing the extent of dark regions in the central image alongside the numerical index may provide useful information for interpreting central visual field status from the AI-CO display.

papers.title: Association of Adduction-Induced Optic Nerve Head Strain with Visual Field Loss Progression in Myopic Normal-Tension Glaucoma: The Wenzhou Glaucoma Progression Study
papers.abstract: PurposeTo characterize the biomechanical response of the optic nerve head (ONH) in myopic versus non-myopic individuals with normal-tension glaucoma (NTG), and to evaluate the association between ONH strains and the rate of visual field (VF) progression. DesignRetrospective clinical cohort study. ParticipantsA total of 118 NTG eyes from 77 patients with [≥] 2 years of follow-up and 5 VF tests were enrolled, including 66 eyes with myopia and 52 eyes without. MethodsEach participant underwent three-dimensional (3D) optical coherence tomography (OCT) imaging of the ONH under three mechanical loading conditions: 20{degrees} adduction, 30{degrees} abduction and acute intraocular pressure (IOP) elevation by applying a 0.80 N force to the lower eyelid. Effective strains across the global ONH complex and within specific segmented tissues (pre-lamina, lamina cribrosa, choroid, and sclera) were quantified using a validated 3D strain-mapping algorithm. ResultsMyopic NTG eyes exhibited significantly higher ONH strains compared to non-myopic eyes under acute IOP elevation (10.1{+/-}2.7% vs. 9.3{+/-}1.8%, P = 0.044) and abduction (9.2{+/-}2.3% vs. 8.4{+/-}2.1%, P = 0.048). In the non-myopic group, ONH strains varied significantly across conditions (P < 0.001), with adduction (9.9{+/-} 2.0%) and acute IOP elevation (9.3{+/-}1.8%) eliciting greater strains than abduction (8.4{+/-}2.1%). These condition-dependent variations were less pronounced in the myopic group (10.1{+/-}2.7% vs. 9.8{+/-}2.7% vs. 9.2{+/-}2.3%, P = 0.07). Multivariable linear mixed-effects analysis revealed that in myopic NTG, higher ONH strains induced by adduction were significantly associated with faster MD decline (estimate: -0.139 dB/year per 1% increase, P = 0.03, adjusted for age, spherical equivalent and baseline perimetric mean defect). Conversely, larger strains during acute IOP elevation were associated with slower progression (estimate: 0.184 dB/year per 1% increase, P = 0.004). Tissue-specific analysis confirmed that adduction-induced strains in the choroid and pre-lamina tissue as well as IOP-induced strains across all ONH tissues were significantly correlated with the rate of perimetric progression in myopic eyes (all P < 0.05). ConclusionsIn this cohort, greater adduction-induced ONH strain was associated with faster perimetric deterioration in myopic NTG. These findings support further investigation of gaze-related optic nerve traction as a potential non-IOP-related biomechanical factor in myopic NTG.

papers.title: Genetically modified cones rescue visual function in children
papers.abstract: Gene therapy can restore retinal signals absent since birth in animal models, yet the translation to humans remains challenging. An unresolved possibility is that meaningful retinal rescue already occurs in humans, but its impact is masked by downstream neural bottlenecks shaped by long-term deprivation. Tracing restored signals through the visual system is therefore essential to distinguish rescue and constraints. We address this challenge in CNGA3-associated achromatopsia, in which retinal cone photoreceptors are present but non-functional from birth. We used tests specifically targeting cone-mediated processing to trace signals from genetically modified cones from the retina to visual cortex and perception. After treatment in late childhood, we find clear evidence of new cone signals reaching visual cortex in 4 out of 7 patients. These signals were replicable over years, retinotopically organised, available for conscious perception and showed higher temporal resolution. Recovery of foveal acuity and canonical colour vision remained limited, consistent with neuroplasticity constraints on specialised neurocircuitry beyond critical developmental windows. Together, these findings show that the human brain can incorporate a new sensory signal after years of complete congenital deprivation, while revealing selective bottlenecks that limit full visual recovery. They provide a framework for optimising sensory restoration: measure rescued input, trace downstream integration of signal, and tailor treatment timing and rehabilitation to maximise functional gain.

papers.title: A Distinct Delayed-Onset Intraocular Inflammation Phenotype of Faricimab versus Aflibercept and Ranibizumab: Triangulated Pharmacovigilance Evidence from Databases of US, Europe and Japan
papers.abstract: PurposePost-marketing reports have associated faricimab, the first intravitreal bispecific antibody, with intraocular inflammation (IOI). Its inflammatory phenotype, temporal pattern, and systemic safety relative to established anti-VEGF agents remain unclear. We compared faricimab with aflibercept and ranibizumab across three independent pharmacovigilance databases. DesignTriangulated Pharmacovigilance study. MethodsWe analyzed FAERS reports (Q1 2022-Q2 2026) with external validation in JADER (Japan) and EudraVigilance (Europe). After de-duplication and restriction to primary-suspect reports, we computed reporting odds ratios (RORs) with false discovery rate control, derived confounder-adjusted RORs by logistic regression, modeled time-to-onset (TTO) with Weibull distributions, and graded signals with a pre-specified bidirectional cross-database evidence framework. ResultsThe FAERS cohort comprised 6,833 faricimab, 6,714 aflibercept, and 2,533 ranibizumab reports. Faricimab showed higher reporting of anterior-chamber and vitreal inflammation: adjusted RORs (comparator versus faricimab; values <1 indicate faricimab excess) were 0.27 (95% CI 0.18-0.40) for iridocyclitis and 0.45 (0.35-0.58) for uveitis versus aflibercept, and 0.13 (0.06-0.24) and 0.12 (0.06-0.20) versus ranibizumab. All four core IOI preferred terms were Confirmed in JADER against both comparators. Faricimab IOI arose late (median TTO 100 vs 7 days; P = 2.6E-14) with a markedly flatter Weibull distribution (shape 0.81 vs {approx}0.42). Aflibercept predominated for endophthalmitis-spectrum and intraocular pressure events; ranibizumab for vitreous hemorrhage (confirmed in JADER). Faricimab showed lower reporting across cardiac, nervous system, vascular, and renal organ classes, confirmed in EudraVigilance. An unadjusted death signal did not survive adjustment and was absent in outcome-based JADER analyses. ConclusionsFaricimab exhibits a reproducible, delayed-onset, anterior-predominant IOI phenotype alongside a comparatively favorable systemic safety profile. Clinicians should recognize that faricimab-associated IOI may arise weeks to months after injection. HighlightsFaricimab showed higher reporting of anterior and intermediate intraocular inflammation than aflibercept and ranibizumab across three independent databases. Faricimab-associated inflammation arose late, with a median onset of 100 days versus 7 days for the comparators. Aflibercept predominated for endophthalmitis-spectrum events and ranibizumab for vitreous haemorrhage. No drug showed excess death reporting after adjustment and outcome-field verification.

papers.title: Advancing genetic pathogenicity prediction with three-dimensional proteoform-phenotype analysis
papers.abstract: Ascertaining the pathogenicity and clinical relevance of genetic mutations is a longstanding challenge across human disease. This is particularly relevant for genes with many variants of unknown significance (VUS), such as PRPH2-retinopathy, where complex variable phenotype patterns and limited genotype correlations hinder application of precision-medicine therapies. Recent AI-based pathogenicity tools, while powerful, may be limited by insufficient mechanistic or phenotypic training data. We established a three-dimensional proteoform-phenotype analysis framework by combining AI-generated protein structural models with clinical genomics data, in which expert consensus adjudicates model outputs through a human-in-the-loop AI approach, to evaluate 46 curated pathogenic missense variants against a background VUS pool. The framework was prospectively validated using an independently evaluated clinical patient cohort. This analysis resolved spatial biophysical signatures corresponding to distinct clinical phenotypes (i.e., retinitis pigmentosa, macular dystrophy, and pattern dystrophy) as well as complex blended presentations. Leveraging these confirmed structural signatures, we prioritized high-risk VUS. This mechanism-resolved framework can be extended to other therapeutically actionable genes to identify novel causal variants and improve diagnosis, prognosis, and better select rare, eligible patients for emerging molecular gene therapy trials. Plain Language SummaryDistinguishing disease-causing mutations from benign ones remains a major barrier to precision medicine. Here, the authors combine AI-generated protein structures with clinical data and expert human adjudication to show that where a PRPH2 variant sits in three-dimensional space predicts the specific retinal disease it causes, enabling variant prioritization for gene-therapy trials

papers.title: Intracortical microstimulation evokes diverse electrode-specific phosphenes in the early visual cortex of blind individuals
papers.abstract: PurposeElectrical stimulation of the occipital cortex evokes visual percepts known as phosphenes. To date, most human studies have examined phosphenes elicited by large surface or depth electrodes. These differ considerably from the small penetrating intracortical microelectrodes capable of stimulating highly localized cortical populations that are the basis of current next-generation devices. Here, we provide a detailed characterization of phosphenes evoked by such intracortical microelectrodes. MethodsAs part of the CORTIVIS clinical trial, a Utah Electrode Array with 100 penetrating electrodes was implanted in the early visual cortex of four blind volunteers. Participants completed drawing and description tasks in response to single-electrode stimulation. Two participants also performed forced-choice tasks to determine whether phosphenes elicited by different electrodes could be reliably discriminated. ResultsSingle-electrode stimulation reliably evoked phosphenes in all participants. Most percepts appeared in the contralateral visual field, although two participants reported near-midline ipsilateral percepts. Phosphenes ranged from simple dots to elongated, textured, circular, or otherwise idiosyncratic forms. One participant reported distinguishable phosphene colors, which depended on electrode and amplitude structure and varied across sessions. The two participants tested on forced-choice discrimination could successfully identify electrode-specific phosphenes across multiple sessions. ConclusionsIntracortical microstimulation of the human visual cortex produces phosphenes with diverse, electrode-specific appearances that are recognizable across repeated trials. These findings indicate that penetrating microelectrodes often evoke more structured percepts than simple points or blobs, providing foundational evidence that electrode-specific encoding strategies will be necessary in future visual prosthetic devices.

papers.title: Four-State Hemodynamic Framework for Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: Mathematical Model Integrating Vascular Permeability, Lesion Transmural Pressure, Choroidal Excess Pressure, and Wall Stability
papers.abstract: PurposeTo apply a mathematical model integrating vascular permeability, lesion transmural pressure, choroidal excess pressure, and wall stability to incomplete fluid response and massive submacular hemorrhage in neovascular age-related macular degeneration. MethodsPermeability was calculated from aqueous vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF). Windkessel gave usual lesion pressure from choriocapillaris pressure and high inflow from an arterial-level puncture pressure used as a working value. Choroidal excess pressure was calculated from choroidal thickness and a pachy index as increased outflow resistance. Exudative change used a revised Starling equation scaled to early central-retinal-thickness reduction, with 40-m threshold. A relative rupture-hazard index was calculated from Laplace wall stress and wall stability. VEGF, pressures, and that reduction were from the literature. Pressure was isolated from permeability and choroidal excess. ResultsIn the model, raising lesion pressure from choroidal-excess lesion pressure to high inflow increased untreated exudative change from 150 to 760 m. Residual under saturation was 64 m as a lower-end reference (Monte Carlo 69-286 m; median, 170) and 90 m with high-hazard choroidal excess; both above 40 m. Reducing choroidal thickness in the thickened choroidal-excess state added 13-14 m, smaller than that residual. Lowering lesion pressure from high inflow to usual lesion pressure (21 to 10 mmHg) reduced the index to 0.64 of the high-hazard reference, and to 0.34 with wall stabilization. ConclusionLesion transmural pressure due to high inflow left residual exudation even after permeability suppression with anti-VEGF. Fluid resolution on optical coherence tomography may not parallel a reduction in the rupture-hazard index, depending on wall stability.

papers.title: Intra-Patient Comparison of a Minimally Invasive Lid Treatment and Traditional Blepharoplasty: Patient and Surgeon-Reported Outcomes
papers.abstract: PurposeTo use a minimally invasive lid treatment (MILT) utilizing Compressive Skin Contouring (CoCo) technology to compare patient- and surgeon-reported ecchymosis, edema, and incision appearance following MILT and traditional upper eyelid blepharoplasty (tBULB). MethodsProspective, single-surgeon intra-patient study comparing MILT and tBULB in patients seen for bilateral blepharoplasty. Patients and the operating surgeon rated MILT and tBULB outcomes post-operatively on the day of surgery (T1) and at 2 months (T2) using surveys. Patient photographs taken 3 and 9 days post-operatively were blindly assessed by 3 independent surgeons to compare ecchymosis, edema, and incision appearance on the MILT and tBULB sides. ResultsSeven patients participated in the study. At T1, 6/7 patients reported [≤] ecchymosis and edema, and all patients reported better or equivalent incision appearance on the MILT side compared to the tBULB side. At T2, 6/7 of patients reported [≤] edema; 4/7 reported < ecchymosis and better incision appearance on the MILT side. The surgeon reported < ecchymosis and [≤] edema for 7/7 patients and better or equivalent incision appearance for 6/7 patients at T1; [≤] ecchymosis and better or equivalent incision appearance for 7/7 and [≤] edema for 6/7 patients at T2 on the MILT side. In the blinded evaluation, mean ecchymosis scores were lower, edema scores were lower or equivalent, and incision appearance was better for MILT vs. tBULB at days 3 and 9. ConclusionsIn this intra-patient study, MILT outcomes compared favorably with tBULB, especially for ecchymosis and edema; two important aesthetic measures of patient perception.

papers.title: OphJev: endpoint-aware System One decisions for ophthalmic imaging and clinical text
papers.abstract: Ophthalmic decisions require probabilities tied to a clinical question, a candidate set and an operating policy. We present OphJev, an endpoint-aware System One framework that combines frozen image and text representations, candidate scoring, schema-specific calibration and selective generalist queries for fundus and OCT imaging. Across eight external resources, multiple representation families, three generalist sizes and three seeds, controlled interventions separate the effects of wording, supervision and computation. Schema-aware affine calibration lowers mean held-out Brier loss and selective risk in all eight primary image-text configurations. On HYGD, matched-supervision fusion raises AUROC from 0.772 to 0.798, while a separate gain-routing policy lowers Brier from 0.618 to 0.599 using at most 20% logical generalist image calls. These effects demonstrate complementary decision-level capabilities rather than universal gains: external transfer and larger specialist banks remain cohort dependent. A retrospective text extension evaluates 1,996 clinical notes and 91 ophthalmic questions; validation-based calibration improves note probability scores, while a lexical control remains strong. OphJev provides an auditable decision framework; prospective clinical benefit remains unvalidated.

papers.title: Retinal vascular trajectories and their associations with systemic health in the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging
papers.abstract: Retinal vascular features are proposed biomarkers of systemic health, yet their longitudinal behaviour and relationship to systemic health remain poorly understood. We quantified retinal vascular morphology from serial colour fundus photographs in the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging, including 21,562 participants at baseline with good quality images. On average, vascular complexity and density decreased between baseline visit and follow-up 2 (mean interval 5.7 years), whereas tortuosity, arteriolar widths, and venular widths increased. Baseline vascular features were associated with demographic, cardiovascular, metabolic and behavioural traits, whereas altered longitudinal trajectories were associated principally with older age and higher low-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Within-person increases in mean arterial pressure covaried with lower vascular complexity, density and vessel widths. In survival analyses, independently of baseline vascular features, increases in fractal dimension were associated with lower hazard of subsequent all-cause mortality (hazard ratio = 0.92 per standard deviation, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.86 - 0.98), whereas arteriolar widening was associated with higher mortality (hazard ratio = 1.09, 95% CI = 1.02 - 1.17). No retinal change metric was associated with major adverse cardiovascular events after false-discovery-rate correction. These findings identify retinal vascular remodelling as a dynamic phenotype associated with systemic health and subsequent mortality, and motivate evaluation of multi-time-point retinal imaging in oculomics.

papers.title: Systematic review finds keratoconus AI unproven in fellow eyes with normal topography and tomography
papers.abstract: Published artificial intelligence for keratoconus is unproven in fellow eyes that topography and tomography call normal, the eyes where surgical decisions are made, although it reports near-perfect accuracy for early disease. In a registered systematic review of 573 studies (PROSPERO CRD420261441197), none of 2,035 claim-by-stratum units from 212 adjudicated studies established discrimination in these eyes. Most units (90.0%) answered a different question, never constructed the target population or certified its normality; external validation did not test label generation, and five systematic reviews did not assess it. In a public cohort, a frozen score yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.996 against a same-eye index label and 0.549 against a contralateral proxy; its inputs reconstructed the label-generating index (r = 0.991), so accuracy there measured agreement with the index. Anchor-gap evaluation measures accuracy in these eyes against the contralateral clinical diagnosis.

papers.title: Interpretable Automated Detection and Measurement of Dome-Shaped Macula on Optical Coherence Tomography
papers.abstract: PurposeTo develop an interpretable automated pipeline for dome-shaped macula (DSM) detection and measurement from optical coherence tomography (OCT) B-scans. MethodsWe analyzed one eye from each of 300 children aged 4-18 years in the Shanghai Child and Adolescent Large-scale Eye Study High Myopia (SCALE-HM) cohort (50 DSM-positive; 100 test eyes). A U-Net pretrained on OCTA-500 and fine-tuned on the development set segmented the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) boundary. A geometric module located the apex, fitted a tangent-line baseline, and computed perpendicular height in physical coordinates. An eye was DSM-positive if any gradable B-scan had height[≥] 50 {micro}m. Two masked graders evaluated the test set; a third adjudicated disagreements. ResultsThe area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.927 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.850-0.986), sensitivity was 82.1% (95% CI, 64.4%-92.1%), and specificity was 100% (95% CI, 94.9%-100%) against the adjudicated reference. In concordant-positive eyes, automated height agreed with manual measurements (intraclass correlation coefficient, 0.949; mean absolute error, 6.9 {micro}m; bias, -5.7 {micro}m, versus Doctor A). Mean RPE-boundary error on pediatric test scans was 1.54 {micro}m. ConclusionsThe pipeline may be considered a reliable and reproducible tool for automated DSM detection and height measurement on radial OCT, with each value traceable to land-marks on the source B-scan. External validation across populations, devices, and acquisition protocols is needed. Translational RelevanceThe pipeline provides an objective and reproducible method to detect DSM and quantify dome height, width, and orientation across OCT meridians. Because each measurement can be verified on the source B-scan, it enables standardized DSM assessment.

papers.title: Functional Impact of Macular Atrophy and Fibrosis in Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration by Defect-Mapping Microperimetry
papers.abstract: PurposeTo understand the functional impact of macular atrophy (MA) and fibrosis in eyes with treated neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) based on deep visual sensitivity losses. DesignCross-sectional study. ParticipantsOne-hundred and nine eyes from 97 individuals with nAMD that had been treated for [≥]12 months without significant retinal fluid. MethodsAll participants underwent defect-mapping microperimetry (DMP) testing - a strategy optimized to quantify the spatial extent of deep visual sensitivity losses through single 10 decibel stimuli presentations - where 208 locations were sampled in the central 8{o} radius region. Participants also underwent color fundus photography, fundus autofluorescence and OCT imaging, which were co-registered and manually annotated for MA and fibrosis to determine their two-dimensional pointwise extent at individual test locations, and global extent in the corresponding region where DMP was performed. Main Outcome MeasuresPointwise association between the presence of MA and fibrosis with missing a stimulus on DMP and global association between the extent of MA and fibrosis with the proportion of locations missed (PLM) on DMP. ResultsAt a pointwise level, the presence of MA and fibrosis were independently associated with an increased likelihood of missing a stimulus on DMP (odds ratio = 42.5 and 2.5 respectively; P <0.001 for both). However, at a global level, only an increasing extent of MA was associated with a significantly higher PLM on DMP (P < 0.001), but not fibrosis (P [≥] 0.227). MA extent explained a substantial proportion of the variance in the PLM (R2 = 0.97) and there was a very strong correlation between the two parameters ({rho} = 0.93). ConclusionsThis study confirmed the expected functional impact of MA and fibrosis on DMP testing at a pointwise level. However, it showed at the global level that only the extent of MA, and not fibrosis, was independently associated with functional loss on DMP, and that there was a very strong structure-function correlation based on MA. These findings thus suggest that evaluating MA alone may be sufficient for capturing structural changes strongly associated with the global extent of deep visual sensitivity losses in those with treated nAMD.

papers.title: A Single Suprachoroidal Injection of AXT107 (Gersizangitide), a Multimodal, Long-Acting Integrin-Disrupting Peptide, in Patients with Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: Results of the Phase 1/2a DISCOVER Trial
papers.abstract: Frequent injections remain a substantial burden in the treatment of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD). AXT107 (gersizangitide) is a long-acting, integrin-disrupting peptide designed for suprachoroidal administration. In the phase 1/2a, open-label DISCOVER trial, 15 participants with active nAMD received a single suprachoroidal injection of AXT107 microparticles at 0.125, 0.25, or 0.5 mg and were followed for 40 weeks. Safety and tolerability were the primary outcomes; visual acuity, retinal thickness, and time to protocol-specified rescue anti-vascular endothelial growth factor treatment were exploratory outcomes. No AXT107-related serious adverse events, clinically significant intraocular inflammation, or sustained intraocular pressure elevations were observed. Fourteen eyes met the protocol-specified baseline imaging criterion for efficacy analyses. Among these eyes, two treatment-experienced eyes completed 40 weeks without protocol-specified rescue, and a third first received protocol-specified rescue at week 36. Anatomical improvements were observed in at least one eye in each dose cohort, although responses varied. A single suprachoroidal injection of AXT107 was well tolerated in this small first-in-human study. The exploratory findings warrant evaluation in a controlled trial One Sentence SummarySuprachoroidal AXT107 was well tolerated, with some eyes remaining free of protocol-specified rescue for up to 40 weeks.

papers.title: General-purpose time-series foundation models enable sample-efficient transfer learning in retinal electrophysiology
papers.abstract: Electroretinography (ERG) measures the functional response of distinct retinal cells to light, but was largely displaced by structural imaging in the 2000s. Standardization efforts by the International Society for Clinical Electrophysiology of Vision (ISCEV) began in the late 1980s, and collapsed the rich time-series traces into reproducible components and implicit times. Recent improvements in hardware (RETeval) and software (artificial intelligence) may increase the utility of ERG data. However, no ERG-specific foundation models exist, and there are not enough public datasets to train one. We asked whether time-series foundation models (FMs) trained without ERG-specific pre-training could be adapted through transfer learning. Using two public datasets, PERG-IOBA (pattern ERG with ocular diagnoses), and LEOPs (full-field ERG focusing on Autism Spectrum Disorder, ASD), we interrogated how FMs could improve over smaller within-domain models. We measured the binary (healthy/typically developing vs any annotation) and multiclass (specific family/diagnosis) classification performance of both frozen and fine-tuned FMs, alongside custom autoencoder and multiscale models, using patient-aware splits for cross validation. We benchmark the same architectures against PTB-XL, a large 12-lead ECG corpus, as both a control for each approach and to explore scaling behavior. We show that 1) pre-trained FMs can reconstruct masked traces from all three datasets, 2) frozen and fine-tuned embeddings, especially combined with multimodal metadata through masked autoencoders, performed best on classification tasks. Performance on PTB-XL was maintained down to 300 records, comparable in size to the ERG datasets. We could not reproduce published classification performance on the ASD task. Taken together, these results support general purpose foundation models as a practical approach to ERG analysis.
